authority: City and County of Swansea Council
researched_by: the council's own motorhome and camper van parking page, its parking and car park index pages and its published beach car park list, plus the National Trust's own Rhosili and South Gower Coast page for the land the council does not own
policy_summary:
Swansea has a dedicated motorhome page and it is a refusal, not an offer. The council's own wording: 'Although many of our car parks are open 24 hours, no overnight camping or sleeping is allowed in any type of vehicle.' There are no aires, no designated stopover bays, no trial, and the page states flatly that no fresh water, waste disposal, showers, toilets or hookups are provided anywhere, with a specific warning not to empty toilet cassettes down drains.

Read precisely, this is a ban on SLEEPING rather than on parking. Daytime parking of a motorhome, campervan or caravan is expressly allowed - 'as long as you have a valid ticket for every parking space they take up' - and the enforcement mechanism the page actually names is a penalty charge notice for a long vehicle straddling two bays on one ticket. The council also forbids spreading into an adjacent space with furniture, water containers or barbecues, which is the tell that the real problem being managed is encampment on the Mumbles and Gower seafront car parks rather than vehicle presence.

The practical position on Gower is harder than the council page alone suggests, because the council does not own the best of it. Rhossili - the single biggest draw on the peninsula - is National Trust, and the Trust's published position there is stronger than the council's: 'Overnight parking and camping are not permitted in the car park or on the headland and is a breach of our byelaws.' The Trust charges a motorhome-specific day tariff at Rhossili (GBP5 up to two hours, GBP10 over) while banning the overnight stay outright, and it holds Pennard, Pwll Du, Bishopston Valley, Penmaen, Nicholaston and Whiteford as well. What the council does own on the coast is the Mumbles and south Gower car park strip - Bracelet Bay, Knab Rock, Southend, The Quarry, Langland, Caswell, Port Eynon, Horton - and all of it falls under the blanket no.

Direction of travel: static and closed. Nothing found suggests Swansea has considered the Gwynedd 'Arosfan' aire model or the Anglesey trial that followed it, despite Gower being the UK's first AONB and under directly comparable van pressure. Swansea's answer to the motorhome question is a link to visitswanseabay.com and a list of commercial campsites.
notes:
The interesting thing about Swansea is that it is a well-run, explicit, easy-to-find prohibition with nothing on the other side of the ledger. Gwynedd and Anglesey both paired provision with enforcement; South Ayrshire built the bays because chemical waste was going into the harbour. Swansea has the same pressure - a first-designated AONB, a peninsula of small beach car parks, a city seafront - and has published only the enforcement half. The cassette-down-the-drain warning on the council's own page is evidence the pollution problem exists here too; the response has been to tell people not to, rather than to give them somewhere to empty legally.

Ownership is the thing to check before relying on any Gower record. The council's beach car park list is the authoritative statement of what is actually council: eighteen car parks, and Rhossili is not among them. A user who assumes 'council car park, therefore council rules' at Rhossili is wrong twice over - it is National Trust, and the Trust's Gower ban is byelaw-backed rather than a condition of entry, which is a materially stronger instrument than the Trust's usual national position.

That byelaw wording is worth propagating: data/sites/national-trust.json currently carries an open question asking for the Trust's own published statement, and this Gower page is it.
open_questions: The legal instrument behind the council's overnight sleeping ban. The motorhome page is guidance; no off-street parking places order text was found online, and the page only names a PCN for the two-bays-one-ticket offence, not for sleeping.
Which car parks have height barriers. The council says some do and some do not, declines to list them, and disclaims liability for damage - the same gap Gwynedd leaves.
Which car parks are open 24 hours and which lock overnight. 'Many' are 24 hours; no opening-times page was reachable.

Whether any on-street TRO or PSPO covers overnight motorhome parking on the Mumbles seafront (Mumbles Road, Knab Rock, Bracelet Bay) or on Gower lanes and lay-bys. Nothing found; the byelaws page names no byelaws and refers enquiries to Legal Services.
Enforcement reality on Gower after dark - whether the sleeping ban is patrolled at all outside the city, or is signage only.
Ownership and rules at Three Cliffs, Oxwich and Llangennith car parks, which are estate or commercially run rather than council or National Trust and were not researched here.

Coordinates are ONS postcode centroids for the postcodes the council and the National Trust publish, not surveyed car park entrances. Port Eynon and Rhossili centroids sit a couple of hundred metres from the actual car parks.

sites.name: All City and County of Swansea council car parks
sites.notes: Estate-wide and unambiguous: 'Although many of our car parks are open 24 hours, no overnight camping or sleeping is allowed in any type of vehicle.' Applies to motorhomes, campervans and caravans alike. Daytime parking IS permitted with a valid ticket for every bay the vehicle occupies; a long vehicle on one ticket gets a PCN. No fresh water, waste disposal, showers, toilets or electric hookups at any council car park, and toilet cassettes must not go down the drains. Adjacent spaces may not be used for furniture, water containers or barbecues. CCTV in operation. The instrument is recorded as the off-street parking places order by inference - the published source is council guidance and the order text was not located.
prohibits: furniture, water containers and barbecues in adjacent spaces

sites.name: Rhossili Car Park (National Trust)
sites.search_hint: National Trust car park, Rhossili, Gower SA3 1PR
sites.notes:
NOT A COUNCIL CAR PARK - National Trust, and it is not on the council's published list of eighteen beach and promenade car parks. The Trust's own wording is the strongest found anywhere on Gower: 'Overnight parking and camping are not permitted in the car park or on the headland and is a breach of our byelaws.' Byelaw-backed, not merely a condition of entry, and it extends beyond the tarmac to the headland - so the Worms Head approach is covered too.

The pricing is the sting: the Trust operates a motorhome-specific tariff (GBP5 up to two hours, GBP10 over two hours, against GBP4/GBP8 for cars) on a 24-hour machine, free to members, while banning the overnight stay outright. Paying the over-two-hours rate buys you the day, not the night. Accessible toilets and a Changing Places facility on site.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of the sat-nav postcode the National Trust publishes for the car park; the car park sits a little north-east of the pin

sites.name: Other National Trust car parks on Gower
sites.notes: Beyond Rhossili the Trust holds Pennard, Pwll Du and Bishopston Valley; Penmaen and Nicholaston Burrows; and Whiteford and North Gower including Cwm Ivy. Between them these cover a large share of the peninsula's coastal parking. The Rhossili wording establishes that the Trust treats overnight parking and camping on its Gower land as a byelaw breach; the same is assumed here for the other Gower properties, but each property page was not individually checked - hence medium confidence and no pin.
